article.headline: Wheeler fans 7 straight to open game, Stott hits tiebreaking single as Phillies beat Brewers 6-4
article.description: — Zack Wheeler struck 11, including a franchise-record seven in a row to start the game, and Bryson Stott hit a tiebreaking single with two outs in the eighth inning as the Philadelphia Phillies inched closer to clinching a playoff spot with a 6-4...
article.linkText: Wheeler fans 7 straight to open game, Stott hits tiebreaking single as Phillies beat Brewers 6-4

images.name: Luis Lara hits an RBI single
images.caption: Luis Lara hits an RBI single

article.story: PHILADELPHIA -- — Zack Wheeler struck 11, including a franchise-record seven in a row to start the game, and Bryson Stott hit a tiebreaking single with two outs in the eighth inning as the Philadelphia Phillies inched closer to clinching a playoff spot with a 6-4 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday night. Wheeler reached 2,000 career strikeouts when he fanned Brice Turang to end the first, becoming the 96th pitcher in MLB history to reach the milestone. Brandon Marsh homered, doubled and drove in three runs for Philadelphia, which is tied with Chicago and San Diego at 87-70 for the three NL wild cards — four games ahead of Arizona with five to play. The Phillies hold a tiebreaker over the Padres but not the Cubs. William Contreras had three RBI for NL Central champion Milwaukee. The Brewers, by virtue of Cincinnati's 4-0 win over Atlanta, clinched a bye in the wild-card round and earned home-field advantage for the Division Series. After the Brewers scored twice in the sixth off Wheeler to tie the game at 3, Stott singled to center off Colton Gordon (0-1). Garrett Mitchell’s throw went to third base to try to get Alec Bohm running from first. But the ball ricocheted off Bohm’s foot, and both he and Luis Arraez scored to make it 5-3. Jhoan Duran earned his 33rd save after José Alvarado (5-3) got the final out of the eighth. Wheeler was unhittable at the outset and had sights on Pablo López’s MLB record of nine K’s in a row to open a contest before Cooper Pratt grounded out to third base for the second out of the third inning. Watching Wheeler from the dugout was teammate Aaron Nola, who has a share of the MLB record with 10 consecutive strikeouts of the Mets in 2021. The Brewers dropped to 13-6 this month and were not able to extend their franchise record of 98 wins, set in Sunday’s 3-0 victory at Baltimore. Up next Brewers RHP Logan Henderson (10-3, 2.51 ERA) opposes Phillies RHP Aaron Nola (7-10, 4.49) in the second game of the three-game series on Wednesday night. ------ See AP’s full MLB coverage here
